```json
  "project_id": "github.com/the-cloud-clockwork/agentihooks",
  "state": "admitted",
  "pod_namespace": "swarm-workers",
  "pod_name": "swarm-a1b2c3-0007",
  "pod_uid": null,
  "image_digest": "sha256:<qualified-image-digest>",
  "launch_spec_digest": "sha256:<canonical-launch-spec-digest>",
  "credential_ref": "execution-scoped-reference",
  "brain_id": "swarm",
  "created_at": "2026-10-08T08:00:00Z"
}
```

The controller writes `execution_id` before creating the Pod.
The Pod carries that identity in controller-owned labels or annotations.
A retry first searches for the same execution identity.
A discovered Pod must have a matching immutable launch specification before adoption.
A Pod with a matching name but different UID or launch digest is not the same attempt.
Store the Pod UID immediately after a successful create or reconciliation read.
Do not consider an attempt working merely because its Pod is Running.
The worker must register, prove its launch binding, and obtain current authority.
The controller records the qualified image digest, not only a mutable image tag.
An execution record never contains a provider token value.
The account identity is an opaque routing identifier with an execution-scoped credential reference.
The human agent name remains compatible with current naming and alias rules.
The herdr-safe name is a presentation adapter, not a replacement for the canonical agent name.

### 22.4 ExecutionLease

| Field | Type | Required | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| execution_id | string | yes | Bound to the registered attempt. |
| task_id | string | yes | Bound to the admitted task. |
| generation | positive integer | yes | Monotonically advances for replacement authority. |
| controller_epoch | positive integer | yes | Identifies the current leadership incarnation. |
| owner_identity | string | yes | Authenticated worker identity, not an arbitrary agent label. |
| acquired_at | server timestamp | yes | Set by the authority service. |
| expires_at | server timestamp | yes | Expiry enforced by the authority service. |
| renewal_sequence | integer | yes | Reject an older renewal observation. |
| admission_state | enum | yes | `active`, `draining`, `revoked`, or `expired`. |
| allowed_operations | set | yes | Allowed operation classes for this attempt. |
| credential_generation | integer | yes | Allows revocation during replacement. |

Use an atomic compare-and-update operation to renew a lease.
A client timestamp cannot replace the server expiry calculation.
The release operation verifies both owner identity and generation before removing a claim.
A former owner must not be able to release a successor's claim.
Leadership replacement and task replacement are separate events with separate counters.
An expired controller lease prevents admission of new work until leadership is re-established.
An uncertain network state prevents starting a replacement writer unless the old authority is fenced.
A stale worker may still consume CPU or call an external service with already-issued credentials.
Therefore the implementation must combine cooperative worker shutdown with scoped credential revocation and protected mutation endpoints.
Do not advertise exactly-once behavior for arbitrary shell commands or third-party API effects.
For protected ledger transitions, enforce generation at the service boundary.
For protected repository merge actions, enforce generation in the merge path rather than trusting the agent's prose.
For filesystem edits, keep every attempt in an isolated workspace so an abandoned writer cannot edit a successor's files.

### 22.5 SessionManifest

The manifest belongs to the evidence domain, not to a live-process registry.
It outlives the worker and can outlive the task.
It records where evidence came from and how complete the retained record is.

| Field | Type | Required | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| session_uid | string | yes | Internal globally unique session identity. |
| native_session_id | string | yes | Harness-native conversation identity. |
| harness | enum | yes | Supported provider adapter identifier. |
| source_host_id | string | yes | Stable collector host identity; no IP required. |
| source_generation | string | yes | Changes on truncation, replacement, or incompatible source rewrite. |
| parent_session_uid | string or null | optional | Explicit parent-child session lineage. |
| resumed_from_session_uid | string or null | optional | Resume lineage, not copied transcript duplication. |
| execution_id | string or null | conditional | Required for managed swarm execution. |
| agent_name | string or null | optional | Source actor label at the time. |
| swarm_id | string or null | optional | Swarm affiliation. |
| task_id | string or null | optional | Task affiliation. |
| project_observations | array | yes | Versioned identity observations for this session. |
| first_event_at | timestamp or null | optional | Earliest retained source event. |
| last_event_at | timestamp or null | optional | Latest retained source event. |
| captured_through | cursor | yes | Last source position read successfully. |
| durable_through | cursor | yes | Last source position acknowledged durably. |
| indexed_through | cursor | yes | Last source position available in search. |
| completeness | enum | yes | `complete`, `partial`, `metadata_only`, or `unknown`. |
| missing_ranges | array | yes | Known gaps, including the evidence for each gap. |
| retention_class | string | yes | Applied retention policy identifier. |
| access_scope | object | yes | Enforced read/write policy binding. |
| raw_archive_ref | object or null | conditional | Durable native-source reference when retained. |
| normalized_archive_ref | object or null | conditional | Durable normalized record reference. |
| normalization_version | string | yes | Exact normalizer version. |
| redaction_policy_version | string | yes | Redaction applied before indexing. |

A transcript retained only as a preview is `partial` or `metadata_only`.
Do not label it complete because a vector exists.
A manifest with no retained raw body must not claim native resumability.
The source host identifier must not be a mutable hostname alone when cloned worker images can share that name.
Assign fresh collector identity at runtime, never bake it into the image.

### 22.6 NormalizedEvent

The normalized event model preserves the distinction between human input, agent output, tool interactions, and injected context.
Tool results may contain untrusted remote content and must retain that provenance.
A system-looking string inside a tool result is not a system instruction.
The normalized model supports incremental reading without loading the whole source file.

| Field | Type | Required | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| event_id | string | yes | Stable identity across ingestion retries. |
| session_uid | string | yes | Parent session manifest. |
| source_generation | string | yes | Disambiguates replaced or truncated source files. |
| native_event_id | string or null | optional | Original ID where available. |
| sequence | integer | yes | Stable normalized sequence inside the source generation. |
| byte_start | integer | conditional | Original source range start where meaningful. |
| byte_end | integer | conditional | Original source range end, exclusive. |
| line_start | integer or null | optional | Human-readable source locator. |
| line_end | integer or null | optional | Human-readable source locator. |
| kind | enum | yes | Human, assistant, tool call, tool result, metadata, usage, or control event. |
| timestamp | timestamp or null | optional | Native timestamp when present. |
| parent_event_id | string or null | optional | Causal relation for messages or child events. |
| tool_call_id | string or null | optional | Joins the request and response for one tool invocation. |
| payload | object | yes | Validated normalized payload. |
| original_hash | string | yes | Hash of retained original bytes or explicit unavailable state. |
| normalized_hash | string | yes | Hash after deterministic normalization. |
| trust_class | enum | yes | Human instruction, agent assertion, tool observation, injected memory, or derived summary. |
| project_id | string or null | optional | Exact project at the event. |
| redaction | object | yes | Redaction status and policy, without secret values. |

Do not use display text as the only event identity.
Identical output appearing twice can be two different real events.
Conversely, the same native event replayed after a transport failure must not be stored twice.
The Codex completion summary fallback must not duplicate a message already retained for the same turn.
A chunk boundary must not turn injected memory into an apparent new operator request.
Parent-child references are nullable during out-of-order arrival and reconciled deterministically later.
An unresolved parent is observable; it does not justify dropping the child event.

### 22.7 Transcript ingestion transaction

The ingestion server receives a manifest binding, one or more source segments, and a batch identity.
The batch identity is stable across retries of the same segment set.
The server validates scope before accepting any archive upload reference.
The server verifies segment content hashes before advancing a durable cursor.
Acknowledgement happens only after the durable archive and catalog commit meet the configured durability contract.
Embedding completion is not required for durable acknowledgement.
An ingestion acknowledgement and an indexing acknowledgement are separate values.
The client may discard a local spool segment only after receiving a durable acknowledgement for that segment.
A lost response causes idempotent retry with the same batch identity.
A repeated batch with different bytes is a conflict, not an update.
A source generation change starts a new sequence namespace and does not overwrite the preceding archive.
A partially written final JSONL line remains buffered until it is complete or explicitly recorded as unrecoverable.
An invalid line is quarantined with its source range and reason; following valid lines remain eligible.
An oversized event uses an archive reference and bounded metadata rather than silent truncation.
The server must expose known gaps to both retrieval and the brain extraction consumer.

```json
{
  "schema_version": "2.0",
  "batch_id": "batch-synthetic-0042",
  "session_uid": "session-synthetic-0007",
  "source_generation": "generation-synthetic-01",
  "cursor_before": {"sequence": 119, "byte_offset": 24000},
  "cursor_after": {"sequence": 125, "byte_offset": 25800},
  "segments": [
    {
      "object_ref": "archive://swarm/session-synthetic-0007/segment-0042",
      "sha256": "<segment-sha256>",
      "record_count": 6,
      "byte_count": 1800
    }
  ]
}
```

The server derives `brain_id`, principal, and allowed project scopes from the authenticated execution binding.
A caller-supplied scope field may narrow a request but must never broaden the binding.
The example object reference is a logical reference, not an instruction to fetch an arbitrary URL.

### 22.8 TranscriptChunk

Chunk identity is derived from stable event identities, source generation, chunker version, and content digest.
It is not derived only from a sliding integer offset in the newest retained Redis window.
A chunk references the original retained record ranges.
The search index can be rebuilt from archives and catalog data without invoking a coding agent.
A chunk's embedding model and dimension are versioned explicitly.
Changing embedding model does not delete the canonical transcript.
A dimension migration uses a new index generation and a qualified read cutover.
Chunk text can be shorter than the source body, but the source remains retrievable with its completeness status.
A summary is a derived document linked to its supporting chunks.
Search returns excerpt boundaries and source references rather than inventing an exact quote from a summary.

| Field | Type | Required | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| chunk_id | string | yes | Stable identity under the declared chunker. |
| session_uid | string | yes | Parent session. |
| first_event_id | string | yes | Inclusive first supporting event. |
| last_event_id | string | yes | Inclusive last supporting event. |
| source_generation | string | yes | Source generation. |
| project_id | string or null | yes | Exact scope or explicit unattributed state. |
| brain_id | string | yes | Evidence-domain scope binding. |
| event_kinds | set | yes | Types included in this chunk. |
| text | string or reference | yes | Indexed representation after redaction. |
| content_digest | string | yes | Digest of indexed representation. |
| chunker_version | string | yes | Boundary algorithm version. |
| embedding_model | string | yes when embedded | Model identity, not only provider alias. |
| embedding_dimension | integer | yes when embedded | Validated dimension. |
| index_generation | string | yes | Qualified vector-index generation. |
| first_event_at | timestamp or null | optional | Source interval start. |
| last_event_at | timestamp or null | optional | Source interval end. |
| completeness | enum | yes | Inherited and refined completeness status. |

### 22.9 Search response contract

Search applies authorization and exact project filters before ranking and before returning counts or snippets.
Semantic similarity is a retrieval score, not factual confidence.
Keyword and semantic branches use the same authorization scope.
The caller can request a time window, harness, task, swarm, and project without relying on text substring matching.
Session diversity is a presentation option; it must not permanently hide multiple distinct useful passages in one session.
Every result supplies a stable source locator that can be opened without accessing the original worker filesystem.
A result from incomplete evidence explicitly says so.
A search with no matches is successful empty retrieval, not a reason to search another brain automatically.

```json
{
  "schema_version": "2.0",
  "query_id": "query-synthetic-0019",
  "scope": {
    "brain_id": "swarm",
    "project_id": "github.com/the-cloud-clockwork/agentihooks"
  },
  "index_generation": "session-index-qualified-01",
  "results": [
    {
      "session_uid": "session-synthetic-0007",
      "chunk_id": "chunk-synthetic-0031",
      "harness": "codex",
      "score": 0.82,
      "score_kind": "cosine_similarity",
      "excerpt": "Synthetic example of a previously verified routing constraint.",
      "record_range": {"first_event_id": "event-120", "last_event_id": "event-125"},
      "completeness": "complete",
      "source_ref": "session://session-synthetic-0007/events/event-120..event-125"
    }
  ],
  "next_cursor": null,
  "warnings": []
}
```

The numeric score above is illustrative, not a proposed acceptance threshold.
Ranking thresholds are qualified on the retrieval evaluation set.
The read endpoint rechecks scope even when the reference came from a prior authorized search.
A withdrawn grant can invalidate an older result reference.

### 22.10 CheckpointManifest

A complete checkpoint is a manifest that points to verified artifacts and their restore requirements.
A partly uploaded checkpoint never becomes the latest complete checkpoint.
Uploading the manifest last is the proposed commit convention.
The manifest itself receives a content hash and immutable generation.

| Field | Type | Required | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| checkpoint_id | string | yes | Immutable checkpoint identity. |
| execution_id | string | yes | Source attempt. |
| task_generation | integer | yes | Source write authority generation. |
| checkpoint_sequence | integer | yes | Monotonic within the source attempt. |
| created_at | timestamp | yes | Checkpoint capture time. |
| committed_at | server timestamp or null | yes | Set only when all required objects verify. |
| status | enum | yes | `preparing`, `uploading`, `complete`, or `rejected`. |
| quiescence_method | enum | yes | Harness-supported snapshot, stopped process, consistent export, or partial capture. |
| native_resume_capability | enum | yes | Qualified, unsupported, or unverified. |
| native_harness_version | string | conditional | Needed for native restore compatibility. |
| native_session_id | string or null | conditional | Conversation to restore. |
| project_id | string | yes | Exact source repository. |
| base_commit | string | yes | Git base required for reconstruction. |
| head_commit | string | yes | Source branch head. |
| branch_name | string | yes | Agent branch with validated ownership. |
| staged_patch_ref | object or null | optional | Staged changes not included in a committed Git object. |
| unstaged_patch_ref | object or null | optional | Unstaged tracked-file changes. |
| untracked_archive_ref | object or null | optional | Allowlisted untracked material. |
| git_bundle_ref | object or null | conditional | Required when commits are not durably reachable elsewhere. |
| native_session_artifacts | array | conditional | Harness-specific material required for qualified native resume. |
| transcript_durable_cursor | cursor | yes | Evidence safely retained at capture time. |
| handoff_ref | object or null | optional | Human-readable task state and next action. |
| dependencies_manifest | object | yes | Toolchain and lockfile reconstruction information. |
| artifact_hashes | object | yes | Hashes and sizes of referenced objects. |
| exclusions | array | yes | Secrets, caches, unsupported state, and explicit gaps. |
| restore_constraints | array | yes | Version, account, path, and format requirements. |

Do not archive environment-variable dumps.
Do not include all account authentication stores in a native session archive.
Do not assume that copying a live SQLite file produces a consistent database snapshot.
Use the supported backup/export method or an explicitly quiesced capture.
A restore requiring unavailable credentials must stop at an operator-visible decision.
A native session failure must not silently turn into a fresh task execution.
The restored agent rereads authoritative task state before performing a write.
The controller allocates a new execution identity and generation for replacement execution.
Restored conversation identity and new runtime identity are deliberately different concepts.

### 22.11 Brain record scope and evidence

Every knowledge entry has an exact `brain_id`.
Project-scoped knowledge additionally has a canonical `project_id` or explicit project set.
An entry marked fleet-wide still belongs to one brain instance unless a deliberate sharing rule exports it.
An entry's source actor is not its authorization scope.
Every inferred claim retains supporting evidence references and derivation metadata.
The provenance distinguishes operator decisions, tool observations, agent conclusions, and model synthesis.
A model-generated interpretation never silently overwrites the operator's explicit decision.
Evidence unavailable after a retention event is represented as missing, not substituted with a similar session.

| Field | Type | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| knowledge_id | string | Stable entry ID. |
| brain_id | string | Owning brain instance. |
| project_ids | array | Exact authorized project associations. |
| visibility | enum | Project, shared-infrastructure, or operator-private policy. |
| knowledge_kind | enum | Arc, lesson, decision, signal, reference, or synthesis. |
| status | enum | Kind-specific lifecycle with explicit supersession. |
| title | string | Display name, not the sole embedding input. |
| body_ref | object | Full-body durable location. |
| evidence_refs | array | Exact session ranges, code revisions, artifacts, or operator statements. |
| derived_from | array | Previous knowledge entries used in synthesis. |
| derivation_version | string or null | Extraction or synthesis algorithm version. |
| author_principal | string | Recorded source author. |
| approved_by | string or null | Approval authority where the lifecycle requires it. |
| last_verified_at | timestamp or null | Independent verification time. |
| revision | integer | Concurrency and cache invalidation version. |
| superseded_by | array | Explicit successor entries. |
| sensitivity | enum | Data-handling category. |

### 22.12 Edge contract

An edge is a first-class, directional relation with evidence.
Do not treat graph topology as a substitute for project authorization.
A graph walk checks permission at every visited vertex and every returned relationship.
An edge pointing at a hidden node must not reveal the hidden title or identifier in an error.
The initial implementation supports the existing relation vocabulary and explicit evidence links.
Adding relations such as `contradicts` requires documented semantics and traversal tests.

| Field | Type | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| edge_id | string | Stable edge identity. |
| brain_id | string | Owning brain. |
| source_id | string | Exact source knowledge entry. |
| target_id | string | Exact target knowledge entry. |
| relation | enum | Parent, child, sibling, unblocks, supersedes, related, or approved extension. |
| direction | enum | Explicit directional semantics; never guessed from list order. |
| evidence_refs | array | Why this relation is asserted. |
| confidence_class | enum | Explicit, verified-inferred, or candidate. |
| status | enum | Candidate, active, rejected, or superseded. |
| revision | integer | Concurrency control. |
| created_at | timestamp | Source creation time. |
| verified_at | timestamp or null | Verification event. |

A candidate relation does not automatically become authoritative retrieval guidance.
Structural inverse relations can be derived in a projection instead of stored twice.
An arc pair may legitimately have more than one distinct semantic relation.
Do not discard `supersedes` merely because the same pair also has a structural relation.
Self-links, cycles, and conflicting direction are validated by relation semantics rather than one universal ban.
A parent hierarchy should reject a cycle.
A loose relatedness graph may contain cycles, but traversal still uses visited sets and bounded budgets.
Deduplication keys include the relation when the relation changes meaning.
The migration from the earlier strongest-type-per-pair rule needs an explicit compatibility report.

### 22.13 ContextRequest and ContextPack

A context request asks what the current task needs, not what is globally hottest.
The request carries task facts supplied by the controller and recent local observations supplied by hooks.
The server derives the allowed scope independently of the request text.
Personal and swarm endpoints return their instance identity so the caller can reject a misrouted response.

```json
{
  "schema_version": "2.0",
  "request_id": "context-request-synthetic-0001",
  "brain_id": "swarm",
  "project_id": "github.com/the-cloud-clockwork/agentihooks",
  "execution_id": "exe-synthetic-0007",
  "task_id": "implement-session-ingestion",
  "task_generation": 3,
  "phase": "implementation",
  "lane": "eng",
  "intent": "Implement incremental transcript ingestion with durable acknowledgements.",
  "subsystems": ["session-catalog", "transcript-normalization"],
  "operation_class": "code-change",
  "budget": {"max_tokens": 3000, "max_graph_depth": 2, "max_items": 12},
  "known_context_revision": null
}
```

`budget` is a caller request bounded by server policy, not permission to exceed service limits.
`operation_class` is validated against the protected transition being requested.
The model cannot self-declare a dangerous operation as harmless to avoid consultation.
A cached pack must match brain, project, task generation, role, phase, policy version, and evidence revision.
Cache entries never key only on a repository basename.

```json
{
  "schema_version": "2.0",
  "brain_id": "swarm",
  "context_id": "context-synthetic-0001",
  "context_revision": "knowledge-revision-0048",
  "task_generation": 3,
  "policy_version": "consultation-policy-01",
  "retrieved_at": "2026-10-08T08:02:00Z",
  "expires_at": "2026-10-08T08:12:00Z",
  "items": [
    {
      "knowledge_id": "lesson-synthetic-archive-ack",
      "kind": "lesson",
      "reason": "Applies to the task's durable-ingestion boundary.",
      "body": "Synthetic example: advance the durable cursor only after verified archive commit.",
      "evidence_refs": ["session://session-synthetic-0002/events/event-8..event-12"],
      "relationship_path": ["arc-synthetic-ingestion", "lesson-synthetic-archive-ack"],
      "status": "active"
    }
  ],
  "omitted": {"budget": 2, "superseded": 1},
  "warnings": [],
  "receipt": "<opaque-server-issued-receipt>"
}
```

The omitted counters cannot reveal hidden-scope populations.
Only counts from the authorized candidate set may be returned.
The context budget must be reconciled with every target adapter's byte and token limits before qualification.
A server budget of several thousand tokens is not satisfied by silently clipping the result to the previous 1536-byte injection cap.
The adapter must either deliver the qualified bounded pack or use a supported staged delivery with explicit completeness.
The receipt is bound to the context digest, not merely a timestamp saying a tool was called.
Delivery acknowledgement records which target hook received the context.
The receipt proves retrieval and supported delivery, not understanding or correctness.
A malicious or mistaken memory item remains retrieved data and never becomes an unconditional tool directive.

### 22.14 ConsultationReceipt

| Field | Type | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| receipt_id | string | Opaque server-issued identity. |
| principal_id | string | Authenticated requesting principal. |
| execution_id | string | Bound worker attempt. |
| task_id | string | Bound task. |
| task_generation | integer | Reject after task replacement. |
| brain_id | string | Exact brain. |
| project_id | string | Exact project. |
| operation_class | string | Permitted consultation transition class. |
| policy_version | string | Rules used to decide sufficiency. |
| context_digest | string | Exact retrieved context. |
| evidence_revision | string | Underlying knowledge revision. |
| result_state | enum | Retrieved, empty, unavailable, or rejected. |
| delivered_at | timestamp or null | Confirmed supported delivery. |
| expires_at | server timestamp | Short bounded validity. |
| override_ref | string or null | Explicit operator override when allowed. |

A fabricated receipt string must fail verification.
A receipt from one agent cannot satisfy another attempt's requirement.
A successful empty result can satisfy a consultation requirement when policy permits it.
Service unavailable is not equivalent to empty retrieval.
A task phase change can invalidate a previously valid receipt.
A forced operator override is recorded with scope, reason, and expiry.
A receipt does not independently authorize Git merges, infrastructure changes, or destructive operations.

<a id="section-23"></a>

## 23. Persistence and transaction design sketches

These sketches describe required semantics rather than database migrations ready to run.
Actual migrations must follow the owning repository's tested migration framework.
Database schema ownership is explicit so transcript and brain deployments do not migrate each other's tables accidentally.

### 23.1 Canonical versus derived stores

The transcript archive is authoritative for retained source bytes.
The session catalog is authoritative for source identity, ordering, visibility, and archive references.
The semantic index is rebuildable from those stores.
Redis may cache catalog data and coordinate admission but is not the only copy of retained evidence.
The brain's knowledge store is authoritative for approved knowledge records and their revisions.
Brain embeddings are derived search projections.
The edge store is authoritative for approved relations, with an export format that survives backend replacement.
A filesystem vault can remain the human-readable representation, but concurrent writers need one coherent mutation boundary.
A read-modify-write append over a shared file is not treated as a distributed transaction.

### 23.2 Proposed relational key layout

```sql
-- Illustrative design only. Review and implement as repository migrations.
CREATE TABLE session_manifest_v2 (
    session_uid text PRIMARY KEY,
    harness text NOT NULL,
    native_session_id text NOT NULL,
    source_host_id text NOT NULL,
    access_domain text NOT NULL,
    completeness text NOT NULL,
    manifest jsonb NOT NULL,
    revision bigint NOT NULL,
    UNIQUE (access_domain, harness, source_host_id, native_session_id)
);

CREATE TABLE session_segment_v2 (
    session_uid text NOT NULL REFERENCES session_manifest_v2(session_uid),
    source_generation text NOT NULL,
    segment_id text NOT NULL,
    first_sequence bigint NOT NULL,
    last_sequence bigint NOT NULL,
    object_key text NOT NULL,
    sha256 text NOT NULL,
    byte_count bigint NOT NULL CHECK (byte_count >= 0),
    committed_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (session_uid, source_generation, segment_id)
);

CREATE TABLE session_ingest_batch_v2 (
    access_domain text NOT NULL,
    batch_id text NOT NULL,
    payload_digest text NOT NULL,
    response jsonb NOT NULL,
    committed_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (access_domain, batch_id)
);

CREATE TABLE knowledge_edge_v2 (
    brain_id text NOT NULL,
    edge_id text NOT NULL,
    source_id text NOT NULL,
    target_id text NOT NULL,
    relation text NOT NULL,
    status text NOT NULL,
    evidence jsonb NOT NULL,
    revision bigint NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (brain_id, edge_id),
    UNIQUE (brain_id, source_id, target_id, relation)
);
```

The unique keys above are starting contracts, not a substitute for row-level authorization.
Session IDs alone are not globally safe across imported corpora without an access-domain binding.
When a native session is intentionally resumed on another host, preserve internal session lineage rather than duplicating evidence blindly.
A source-host uniqueness rule may therefore need an explicit migration/adoption record for qualified cross-host resume.
Do not infer that migration from a coincidentally matching native UUID.
The implementation must choose and document whether one internal session spans multiple qualified source incarnations or records them as linked sessions.
The default proposed choice is one stable internal session with explicit source-incarnation records after authorized native resume.
The import path uses a mapping table so older identifiers remain resolvable.

### 23.3 Archive commit failure cases

An object upload can succeed while catalog commit fails.
In that case the object is an unreferenced candidate and the client must not advance the durable cursor.
Retrying the same batch can reuse the verified object digest.
An eventual orphan reaper deletes only objects that have remained unreferenced beyond a documented grace interval.
A catalog row must never reference a body that was not verified or durably committed.
If the object store acknowledgement is weaker than the required durability contract, the server must state the weaker guarantee.
Restore verification tests download and hash representative bodies rather than trusting storage metadata alone.
A database restore to an earlier point must not make newer object evidence disappear silently.
Reconciliation can discover orphaned newer objects, but only through validated manifests and provenance.
An archive object name must not contain credentials or raw user prompts.

### 23.4 Index update failure cases

An embedding API timeout does not roll back a durable transcript commit.
The segment remains visible through direct source retrieval while semantic indexing is pending.
Index state records its last successful input digest and model generation.
Unchanged chunks do not require new embeddings.
Partial batch success records successful chunk IDs and retries only missing work.
A model dimension mismatch rejects the embedding write before corrupting the active index.
A new index generation is built alongside the previous qualified generation.
Cutover requires retrieval evaluation and completeness checks.
Rollback switches the read generation without deleting the canonical archive.
A derived-index rebuild must not trigger execution of transcript commands or automatic agent launches.

### 23.5 Brain mutation concurrency

Two marker writes for one daily log must not overwrite each other.
Prefer a transactional record store or a single serialization point with explicit idempotency.
Generate decision IDs atomically instead of scanning filenames and picking the next number without a lock.
A marker idempotency key is scoped to principal, brain, and payload digest.
An identical key with different content is rejected.
A knowledge edit includes an expected revision.
A failed revision comparison returns the current revision without leaking unauthorized content.
Synthesis operates on a snapshot of source revisions.
Before applying synthesis, verify that the relevant source revisions have not changed incompatibly.
A synthesis candidate based on superseded evidence is retained as a candidate or recomputed, not silently promoted.

<a id="section-24"></a>

## 24. Runtime transition and race catalogue

### 24.1 Admission before Pod creation

The controller reads the current task state and eligibility under the existing lane and territory rules.
It evaluates global account quota, active execution caps, pending execution caps, and budget policy.
It reserves the task generation and account slot atomically or through a documented compensating transaction.
It stores the immutable launch intent.
Only then does it create the execution Pod.
If Pod creation fails definitively, the controller releases the reservation after checking that no matching Pod exists.
If creation is ambiguous, the controller reconciles by execution identity.
It does not generate a second attempt merely because the create response timed out.

### 24.2 Registration before running the harness

The worker validates required files, supported harness versions, and the launch manifest.
It starts local runtime supervision and readiness checks.
It registers with the controller using the execution-scoped identity.
It receives or renews current task authority.
It prepares the repository and worktree from approved sources.
It starts transcript capture before launching the agent conversation.
It obtains the task-start context pack or the explicit allowed degraded decision.
It launches the harness in the headless herdr runtime.
It marks the execution working only after the launch identity and conversation binding are confirmed.
If any required stage fails, it reports the exact stage and does not claim useful work began.

### 24.3 Client and transport disconnect

An operator viewer closing only changes viewer connectivity state.
It does not revoke task authority or shut down the worker.
The private terminal tunnel may reconnect to the same runtime target.
The connection manager resolves the current Pod UID and server identity before sending commands.
A stale connection to an old Pod is discarded, not reused because the Pod name was recycled.
The controller distinguishes viewer loss, terminal transport loss, worker heartbeat loss, and Pod termination.
Only the latter observations participate in the execution failure policy.

### 24.4 Controller restart during launch

Persisted launch intents remain visible after the controller restarts.
The new controller obtains a new leadership epoch.
It lists execution Pods under its allowed label selector.
It matches each Pod to an intended execution record and immutable launch digest.
It adopts only matching current attempts.
It quarantines or terminates unowned execution Pods through an explicit policy after audit.
It does not adopt unrelated Pods merely because they contain the same image.
Worker heartbeats from an older epoch are either reauthorized deliberately or rejected.
A replacement controller cannot assume every Running Pod still has valid task authority.

### 24.5 Worker partition with an otherwise healthy node

The worker tracks the last authority renewal using a monotonic local clock.
Before its allowed grace window ends, it stops admitting new protected mutations.
It attempts to flush evidence and checkpoint material to permitted durable services.
It reports connectivity state if any control channel is still available.
The controller does not immediately create a replacement merely because one heartbeat is late.
It waits for the documented failure condition and fences the old generation before admitting a replacement.
The private worktree prevents the old process from changing the new attempt's filesystem.
Central ledger and merge endpoints reject the old generation.
External API effects that cannot be fenced remain an explicitly documented uncertainty.
The recovery UI identifies this ambiguity rather than claiming all prior effects are absent.

### 24.6 Graceful drain

The controller marks the execution draining and stops assigning new work to it.
The worker reaches a bounded safe point or reports that it cannot do so within the available deadline.
It persists the latest transcript segments.
It checkpoints recoverable source changes and the native session state when qualified.
It uploads the checkpoint manifest only after referenced objects verify.
It reports the completed checkpoint identity and accepted durable cursor.
The controller records the handoff and releases current authority only through an ownership-checked transition.
The runtime supervisor terminates remaining owned processes and exits.
A drain timeout is not treated as completed checkpointing.

### 24.7 Spot interruption and abrupt loss

A Spot notice may provide a short interruption window, but the system must also handle immediate or unobserved loss. [SRC-AWS-SPOT]
The worker cannot rely solely on a termination hook for all persistence.
Periodic transcript spooling and checkpoints bound recoverable loss before any notice arrives.
The termination handler drains according to the existing infrastructure policy.
The workload uses the smaller of its configured shutdown budget and the actual available infrastructure deadline.
A longer Pod termination grace setting does not extend the lifetime of an EC2 instance that is being reclaimed.
After loss, the controller reports the latest complete checkpoint and durable evidence cursor.
Missing recent edits or transcript tail data remain explicitly unknown or lost.
A replacement uses a new task generation.
A native resume is attempted only when its compatibility and artifact prerequisites pass.
Otherwise the operator or policy chooses context continuation or fresh execution explicitly.

### 24.8 Completion with an uncertain external effect

A successful local command return does not prove a remote merge or artifact upload committed.
The completion path queries the remote system using the stable operation reference.
If the state is ambiguous, task completion remains pending verification.
Do not repeat a non-idempotent effect automatically just to obtain a clean response.
The outcome record includes the evidence used to resolve ambiguity.
A later confirmation updates the same operation record.
The task's proof contract remains independent of the terminal process exit code.

### 24.9 Pause, stop, and emergency actions

Pause prevents new admissions while current authorized work may continue.
Drain requests bounded checkpoint-and-stop behavior.
Stop-now revokes authority and terminates the identified runtime with explicit data-loss risk.
An emergency shared-infrastructure signal follows the operator-approved policy; retrieved historical text cannot invoke it.
Every action shows affected tasks and execution identities before a human confirms a destructive operation.
The API verifies action authorization even when the UI already checked it.
A stale UI card cannot terminate a successor that reused the same display name.
An emergency action must not silently delete durable transcript or checkpoint evidence.

<a id="section-25"></a>

## 25. Proposed configuration, image, and deployment examples

All examples in this section are design shapes to implement and qualify.
They are not commands that exist today unless the text explicitly says so.
Secrets are referenced by identity; their values never belong in the plan or image.

### 25.1 Controller configuration shape

```yaml
schema_version: "2.0"
controller:
  enabled: false
  identity: swarm-controller
  execution_backend: local
  leadership:
    required_for_admission: true
    fence_on_epoch_change: true
  admission:
    max_active_executions: 4
    max_pending_executions: 4
    reject_unknown_runtime_profile: true
  credentials:
    issue_execution_scoped: true
    expose_account_inventory_to_workers: false
  ledger:
    endpoint_ref: ledger-api
    auth_ref: ledger-controller-credential
  sessions:
    endpoint_ref: session-api
    archive_ref: transcript-archive
    require_durable_ack: true
  brain:
    routing_policy_ref: approved-brain-routing
  kubernetes:
    namespace: swarm-workers
    pod_template_ref: qualified-swarm-worker
    allow_host_network: false
    allow_host_pid: false
    allow_privileged: false
```

The small execution caps above are proposed canary values, not measured production capacity.
Actual accepted values live in the deployment policy and are recorded in release evidence.
Admission caps count active and starting attempts consistently across controller restarts.
A pending cap is separate so an infrastructure outage cannot create an unbounded Pod backlog.
Account limits are separate from Pod and node limits.

### 25.2 Brain routing configuration shape

```yaml
schema_version: "2.0"
brains:
  personal:
    endpoint_ref: personal-brain-api
    credential_ref: personal-brain-client
    allow_automatic_export: false
  swarm:
    endpoint_ref: swarm-brain-api
    credential_ref: swarm-brain-client
    allow_automatic_export: false
routing:
  explicit_session_binding_first: true
  managed_swarm_default: swarm
  personal_session_default: personal
  missing_binding: reject_scoped_mutation
  cross_brain_fallback: disabled
context:
  task_start: required
  first_write_after_task_change: required
  architecture_transition: required
  refresh_on_evidence_revision: true
  lookup_on_every_tool_call: false
  require_delivery_receipt: true
learning:
  outcome_record: required
  novel_lesson: optional
  accept_no_new_learning: true
```

An explicit session binding must still be authorized for the caller.
It does not let a swarm worker opt into the personal brain by changing its environment.
The private default belongs to personal execution environments, not to every machine by name.
A client can use a local brain and a remote brain in separate sessions without simultaneously running both stacks on the same host.
Same-host multi-instance support requires the lifecycle changes in the MUL workstream.

### 25.3 Worker environment contract

| Variable category | Provisioning | Worker authority |
|---|---|---|
| Execution identity | Controller-signed launch manifest | Read its own binding only. |
| Swarm/task/lane | Launch manifest and compatible existing environment fields | Cannot choose a different task generation. |
| Project identity | Launch manifest plus deterministic local validation | Can report mismatch, not broaden scope. |
| Harness account | Scoped secret reference | Exactly the selected account or approved broker credential. |
| Ledger endpoint | Service discovery/configuration | Authenticated task-scoped operations. |
| Session ingestion endpoint | Service discovery/configuration | Write its own evidence; scoped reads where granted. |
| Brain endpoint | Session binding | Read/write the selected brain under policy. |
| Git identity | Qualified configuration | Commit identity is not repository authorization. |
| Build service | Optional authenticated remote build configuration | No host Docker socket by default. |
| Telemetry endpoint | Qualified configuration | Emit sanitized operational data. |

Do not bulk-inject the controller's complete environment into the worker.
Do not inject every available Claude or Codex account token into each Pod.
Do not copy the operator's whole SSH directory.
Do not expose cluster bootstrap secrets to an execution container.
The worker should not need direct credentials to change ASG desired capacity.
Where the current launcher expects a named account variable, provide only that selected variable in its supported format.
Account-variable compatibility is implemented inside the launcher adapter, not by exposing the entire account inventory.

### 25.4 Worker image build contract

The image is built from a reviewed minimal supported Linux base.
Pin the base image by digest for a qualified release.
Pin the qualified herdr, Claude, Codex, Python, Node, and package-manager versions.
Record the version matrix in the image labels or a bundled machine-readable manifest.
Install the agentihooks code at an immutable revision or released package version.
Install the approved profile, hooks, rules, skills, and local MCP dependencies during the build.
Secrets, account logins, machine IDs, and session history are not build inputs.
Runtime initialization may materialize per-attempt settings from those immutable assets.
Runtime initialization must not `git pull` an unreviewed branch or upgrade the entire toolchain.
Use a non-root runtime identity.
The image entrypoint supervises the herdr server and one managed main harness process.
The exact init/supervisor choice is qualified by signal-forwarding and child-reaping tests.
A PID-1 wrapper that waits forever after the managed workload has died is not a healthy execution runtime.
Readiness includes execution registration and required local runtime readiness.
Liveness does not treat a temporary brain or embedding outage as a reason to kill a productive agent.

| Dependency | Baseline inclusion | Qualification |
|---|---|---|
| herdr | Required | Headless launch, remote attach, pane identity, shutdown. |
| agentihooks | Required | Full target-specific hook installation and task lifecycle. |
| Claude CLI | Required for supported Claude lane | Hook compatibility and native-session artifact handling. |
| Codex CLI | Required for supported Codex lane | Hook delivery capability and transcript normalization. |
| Git and gh | Required | Clone, branch, PR, and authenticated operation behavior. |
| Python and uv | Required | Repository tooling without mutating an unrelated shared environment. |
| Node and package manager | Required for approved frontend/tooling tasks | Explicit versions and lockfile behavior. |
| Shell utilities and process inspection | Required | Bootstrap diagnostics, archive operations, local process identity. |
| Browser automation | Profile-dependent | Headless browser, fonts, libraries, sandbox policy, screenshot artifacts. |
| Container build client | Profile-dependent | Remote authenticated build service; no privileged nested daemon by default. |
| AWS CLI | Profile-dependent | Scoped workload credentials only. |
| Terraform and kubectl | Profile-dependent | Read-only or explicitly delegated infrastructure authority. |
| Language compilers | Profile-dependent | Added only for declared repository requirements. |

A single image can provide these qualified profile-dependent tools without enabling their credentials.
Adding a tool does not grant permission to use it against production.
Keep the first image broad enough for the existing swarm's real repositories, but avoid bundling complete database or brain stacks.
A later image split needs evidence that size or incompatible dependencies justify the additional maintenance burden.

### 25.5 Proposed execution Pod shape

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: swarm-synthetic-attempt
  namespace: swarm-workers
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: swarm-worker
    app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: agentihooks
    swarm.agentihooks/execution: exe-synthetic-0007
  annotations:
    swarm.agentihooks/launch-digest: "<qualified-launch-digest>"
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  automountServiceAccountToken: false
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 90
  securityContext:
    runAsNonRoot: true
    runAsUser: 1000
    runAsGroup: 1000
    fsGroup: 1000
  containers:
    - name: worker
      image: ghcr.io/the-cloud-clockwork/swarm-node@sha256:<qualified-image-digest>
      securityContext:
        allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
        capabilities:
          drop: ["ALL"]
      resources:
        requests:
          cpu: "1"
          memory: 2Gi
          ephemeral-storage: 8Gi
        limits:
          memory: 6Gi
          ephemeral-storage: 30Gi
      volumeMounts:
        - name: runtime-home
          mountPath: /home/swarm
        - name: workspace
          mountPath: /workspace
        - name: execution-config
          mountPath: /run/swarm-config
          readOnly: true
  volumes:
    - name: runtime-home
      emptyDir: {}
    - name: workspace
      emptyDir: {}
    - name: execution-config
      secret:
        secretName: execution-scoped-config
```

This template intentionally omits live credentials, addresses, node tolerations, and an invented executable command.
The image's qualified entrypoint supplies the actual supervised command contract.
The launch renderer adds the correct admission-approved affinity and tolerations.
The example request and limit values are experiments, not production sizing evidence.
The emptyDir volumes are explicitly ephemeral; the archive and checkpoint contracts are mandatory before loss-tolerant rollout.
The Pod does not receive a Kubernetes API token by default.
If a narrowly scoped API call is unavoidable, define a dedicated service account and explicit RBAC rather than reusing controller credentials.
An SSH helper requiring elevated startup privileges needs an explicit reviewed exception or a separate restricted transport design.
Do not silently weaken the non-root/capability policy just to make a generic sshd configuration start.
A private SSH transport can use a qualified non-root server configuration, or a restricted relay into the Pod's supported runtime path.
The chosen transport must be proven in HDR before one-window terminal control is declared complete.

### 25.6 Node placement contract

The baseline canary uses only explicitly approved existing placement classes.
The current CI-related AWS taints remain opt-in.
No change to existing runner tolerations is needed merely to add a new swarm Pod template.
A swarm that uses existing CI capacity must have an explicit shared-capacity policy and budget.
Research capacity remains separate unless the operator approves a policy change with regression evidence.
A proposed Spot-specific worker profile can require Spot eligibility when its recovery contract is qualified.
An on-demand-only profile must not acquire Spot tolerations through a common template merge accidentally.
A `prefer-spot` profile describes scheduler preference, not a promise about which ASG the autoscaler expands.
A pool-expansion preference change belongs to antoncore and needs cluster-wide impact review.
The master/controller and durable evidence services remain on stable, explicitly approved capacity.
Do not place the controller on a node that its own infrastructure dependency may scale down without a qualified availability design.

### 25.7 Configuration precedence and restart policy

Controller policy and authenticated launch binding define non-overridable security scope.
Operator deployment values define permitted resource classes and endpoints.
Repository configuration may choose an allowed profile but cannot grant a broader account or brain scope.
Session-local configuration may narrow or request a permitted choice.
Provider-specific settings are generated through the existing target adapter.
A conflicting configuration returns an explicit error rather than silently selecting the least restrictive value.
A versioned configuration hash is recorded on every admitted attempt.
Changing global configuration affects future attempts unless an explicit live-update protocol exists.
An automatic image or Secret reloader must not restart all active workers without a drain policy.
Credential expiry and revocation are handled by the worker/control protocol, not by indiscriminate rolling restarts.
A brain endpoint or brain identity change invalidates the affected context caches and receipts.
A changed routing file must not silently rebind a live personal session to the swarm brain.
<a id="section-26"></a>

## 26. Implementation execution guide for the swarm master

### 26.1 First action when the implementation issue is picked up

Read sections 0 through 4 before assigning work.
Read the source baseline and refresh the three `dev` heads.
Record which code revision is actually deployed where authorized read access is available.
Do not equate a current repository head with the deployed system.
Open the existing brain project-scoping issue and confirm its current status before duplicating work.
Create one umbrella ledger for this program and link the implementation issue.
Use this plan's stable package IDs as the external requirement keys.
Import the workstream dependency graph rather than inventing a second ordering system.
Split each work package into smaller engineering tasks only when necessary for reviewable changes.
Keep the original package ID on every split task and its pull request.
Do not assign all 150 packages simultaneously.
Start with the source baseline, identity contracts, and local compatibility seam.
Allow mocked consumer work in parallel only after the producer's contract is agreed.
Do not unblock live rollout from a mock alone.
Keep a separate status for contract-ready, implemented, tested, live-qualified, and accepted.
A green unit test does not imply live qualification.
A successful live demo does not excuse a failing scope or recovery test.

### 26.2 Repository task ownership

`agentihooks` owns the worker image source, runtime adapters, controller integration, ledger changes, session catalog, transcript capture, semantic search, brain routing, and execution gates.
`agentibrain-kernel` owns project-aware knowledge, extraction from canonical evidence, graph relations, active context selection, full-detail retrieval, and isolated named brain instances.
`antoncore` owns the deployment manifests, private connectivity, existing ASG integration, capacity policy, service placement, operational secrets delivery, and infrastructure runbooks.
Cross-repository packages publish a producer contract before a consumer enables it.
The deployment owner records exact image digests and configuration revisions for live tests.
The operator-facing ledger links changes in all three repositories without pretending they are one atomic Git commit.
A package can be complete in source while its deployment gate remains closed.
When one repository is unavailable, work in other repositories may continue against qualified fixtures, but integration remains visibly blocked.

### 26.3 Suggested initial parallel tracks

Track A establishes baseline and identity contracts in FND and IDN.
Track B preserves and tests the local runtime seam in RUN after the relevant IDN contract exists.
Track C prepares the immutable worker image in IMG against the agreed runtime launch contract.
Track D prepares session-source fixtures for SES without running a second production collector yet.
Track E refreshes issue 89 and develops BRP against the canonical identity fixture.
Infrastructure discovery in antoncore may run read-only during these tracks.
Live infrastructure mutation waits for the explicit capacity and containment gates.
After CTL, LDG, and IMG are tested, KUB and HDR can converge on one non-Spot worker.
After SES and IDX are qualified, MIG can backfill and compare historical retrieval.
After BRP, GRF, and CTX converge, GAT can validate real delivery receipts.
MUL can develop independently after its identity and scope contracts exist.
CKP must qualify before Spot workloads are treated as recoverable.
OBS should be integrated early enough to collect meaningful evidence for every live gate.
The final REL acceptance includes CAP, ACC, ING, and UX as well as tests, deployment, retention, operations, and migration.

### 26.4 How an engineer reads the large plan

Do not inject the entire plan into every agent's startup context.
Provide the assigned package, its direct dependency contracts, relevant core sections, and its three conformance scenarios.
Provide source URLs and tested commit identifiers with that context bundle.
The full plan remains available for explicit lookup by section or package ID.
The master maintains the global dependency view and cross-repository ordering.
An engineer does not need every runbook or every unrelated test in its context window.
The initial task prompt should identify the exact repository, current worktree, package ID, owned paths, proof contract, and expected artifacts.
After a handoff, the successor rereads the current ledger and package evidence, not only the previous agent's summary.
Do not allow an old cached plan excerpt to override a later accepted plan revision.
Every evidence record identifies the plan revision used to define the test.

### 26.5 Worktree and integration discipline

Create an isolated worktree for each engineering cycle using the existing repository-supported workflow.
Preserve the current base-branch policy unless the operator explicitly changes it.
Do not edit the primary checkout concurrently from multiple agents.
Do not reuse one worktree across two execution attempts after a failure.
A repository clone on a worker is local to that attempt or an explicitly managed safe cache.
GitHub branches and pull requests are source integration mechanisms, not live task-ownership locks.
The ledger's territory and dependency model still governs parallel edits.
A cross-repository task records the compatibility order before merging producer and consumer changes.
Do not deploy a consumer requiring new authority fields before the producer validates and emits them.
Keep additive compatibility until the migration gate has evidence for removing old behavior.
Shared infrastructure templates require a focused diff; avoid opportunistic unrelated cleanup during swarm rollout.

### 26.6 Required package handoff record

```json
{
  "package_id": "SV2-SES-03",
  "plan_revision": "<plan-commit-or-download-sha256>",
  "repository": "the-cloud-clockwork/agentihooks",
  "tested_commit": "<commit>",
  "status": "implemented-not-live-qualified",
  "interfaces_changed": [],
  "migrations": [],
  "tests": {
    "positive": "evidence/SV2-SES-03/a-result.json",
    "negative": "evidence/SV2-SES-03/b-result.json",
    "recovery": "evidence/SV2-SES-03/c-result.json"
  },
  "known_limitations": [],
  "next_action": "<one concrete verified next step>",
  "rollback_reference": "<reviewed rollback procedure>"
}
```

The example package ID is illustrative; engineers use the package actually assigned to them.
Do not copy the example status into a completion record without changing it to the verified state.
Evidence artifacts must be stored durably and scoped appropriately.
A path printed in a report is not evidence that the file exists.

<a id="section-27"></a>

## 27. Failure-oriented operational runbooks

The runbooks below are proposed operational procedures for the implemented system.
They use logical resource references and existing read-only command shapes where possible.
Mutation commands are intentionally described by validated operation and preconditions rather than invented current CLI syntax.
Every destructive or spend-affecting action requires the applicable operator policy.

### 27.1 Viewer closed but agents should continue

Symptom: the operator terminal is closed or detached.
Expected behavior: worker processes, control heartbeats, and transcript capture continue.
Read the ledger's execution state and latest heartbeat using the authenticated control surface.
Check that viewer connectivity is separate from execution state.
Reconnect the Anton-hosted herdr client to the same managed machine registration.
Verify the remote session and native conversation identity before sending input.
Do not launch a new agent merely because the previous viewer disappeared.
If the worker is alive but the machine profile is absent, reconcile the controller-owned registration.
Do not remove an unrelated manually configured machine profile.
Evidence: same execution identity and conversation before and after viewer reconnection.
Failure containment: disable automatic terminal input for unverified targets while leaving authorized execution running.

### 27.2 One remote terminal cannot connect

Symptom: one worker's terminal endpoint fails while other workers remain reachable.
Check the private transport endpoint, current Pod UID, server incarnation, and SSH trust binding.
Check the worker control heartbeat independently of the terminal path.
Verify that the machine profile points to the intended execution and remote herdr session.
Do not retry an earlier pane mutation automatically after an ambiguous transport response.
Read terminal state first where the operation allows reconciliation.
Do not fall back to Local on any remote-resolution failure.
Keep the affected card marked stale or disconnected until identity is revalidated.
A changed host key requires the qualified rotation path, not a blanket host-key-check bypass.
Evidence: connection diagnostics without credential values and target-resolution records.
Recovery: restore the private route or registration and attach to the same live runtime.

### 27.3 Pending Pod does not trigger scaling

Symptom: a worker Pod remains Pending and no eligible node appears.
Check the scheduler event reason before looking at raw node counts.
Check CPU, memory, ephemeral-storage, required affinity, and every taint/toleration.
Check whether a scale-from-zero node template can satisfy all required constraints.
Check the controller's pending cap and the ASG's current configured ceiling.
Check autoscaler discovery, provisioning timeout, and launch failures through the existing antoncore runbook.
Distinguish an impossible request from temporarily unavailable cloud capacity.
Do not remove workload taints or increase ASG ceilings as an automatic remedy.
Do not repurpose the reserved research pool to satisfy an unrelated swarm request.
Evidence: sanitized scheduler events, autoscaler decision, and the admitted resource specification.
Recovery: correct the swarm-only profile or obtain an explicit capacity-policy decision.

### 27.4 Example read-only Kubernetes diagnosis

The variables below must already point to the explicitly authorized cluster and namespace.
They do not choose a cluster automatically.

```bash
: "${SWARM_CONTEXT:?Set the authorized Kubernetes context}"
: "${SWARM_NAMESPACE:?Set the swarm execution namespace}"
kubectl --context "$SWARM_CONTEXT" -n "$SWARM_NAMESPACE" get pods \
  -l app.kubernetes.io/managed-by=agentihooks -o wide
kubectl --context "$SWARM_CONTEXT" -n "$SWARM_NAMESPACE" get events \
  --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp
```

Do not paste unredacted events into a public issue when they contain sensitive resource names or private source references.
Do not treat all namespace events as proof about one execution; correlate the Pod UID and execution identifier.
A missing namespace or unavailable context is a diagnostic limitation, not evidence that there are zero workers.

### 27.5 Node launched but never becomes usable

Symptom: an ASG instance exists but its expected execution Pod never schedules.
Verify whether the node joined the existing k3s cluster at all.
Use the existing authorized node-bootstrap observation path; do not add bootstrap credentials to worker Pods.
Check private-network reachability to the control plane.
Check the AWS provider identity format and the node's advertised labels and taints.
Check the lifecycle-hook outcome and warm-pool state using the established source-controlled join design.
Do not rewrite the on-prem provider identities to AWS identities.
Do not reboot or replace unrelated healthy nodes while diagnosing one failed canary.
Evidence: join stage, lifecycle state, current node identity, and autoscaler classification.
Recovery: repair the reviewed AMI or bootstrap configuration and qualify a fresh canary.

### 27.6 Worker process alive but authority expired

Symptom: the process is still running but the controller rejects generation-bound writes.
Check the worker's last accepted renewal and the controller's current task generation.
Check whether a leadership epoch changed or a successor was admitted.
Stop starting new mutations in the stale worker.
Capture its remaining isolated workspace and transcript as quarantined evidence if policy permits.
Do not merge its branch automatically after a successor has taken ownership.
Do not manually restore its old claim without reconciling the current task owner.
Evidence: old and current generations, rejection reason, and surviving artifact references.
Recovery: retire the stale attempt or route its work as an explicit reviewable candidate to the current owner.
The current owner decides whether any stale work is usable under the proof contract.

### 27.7 Duplicate Pod or ambiguous spawn

Symptom: the controller sees more than one runtime object associated with an expected launch.
Compare execution IDs, Pod UIDs, launch digests, and controller ownership metadata.
A repeated API request for the same execution should converge on one intended Pod.
An unrelated object with the same name is not adopted.
Fence attempts without current task authority before any shared mutation is allowed.
Do not terminate an object based only on its display label.
Retain the create-request and response evidence for the ambiguous operation.
Evidence: object list scoped to the execution and the corresponding persisted launch intent.
Recovery: keep the uniquely admitted attempt and retire only verified unowned or stale attempts through the audited policy.
If ownership cannot be established, pause admissions rather than guessing.

### 27.8 Global account capacity appears wrong

Symptom: the swarm admits too many provider sessions or waits despite available capacity.
Check distributed reservations separately from observed process counts.
Check reservations for starting, active, draining, and handed-off attempts.
Check expiry and reconciliation of reservations belonging to lost workers.
Verify that account identity does not depend on reading the controller host's process table.
Verify that child sessions and background provider daemons follow the intended accounting policy.
Do not print provider token values while identifying the account.
Do not create extra cloud nodes to solve a provider-account quota constraint.
Evidence: account IDs, reservation states, configured caps, and sanitized quota observations.
Recovery: reconcile stale reservations under ownership checks and preserve the provider's actual limits.

### 27.9 Transcript archive lag is growing

Symptom: captured cursor advances but durable cursor falls behind.
Check local spool size, oldest unacknowledged batch, archive availability, and catalog commit failures.
Check whether a source record is too large or a partial final line is blocking a parser incorrectly.
Verify that the retry uses the same batch identity and source generation.
Do not discard the local spool merely because an object upload was attempted.
Do not mark the durable watermark equal to the captured watermark by administrative override.
Apply bounded backpressure when storage is near its safety threshold.
The policy may pause new tasks before evidence loss becomes unavoidable.
Evidence: cursor difference, segment hashes, failed batch stage, and spool capacity.
Recovery: restore the dependency, replay idempotently, and verify retrieved bytes before trimming local segments.

### 27.10 Semantic search misses a known recent session

Symptom: direct transcript retrieval works but semantic search cannot find the session.
Compare durable and indexed watermarks.
Check that the exact project and brain scope match the caller's authorized request.
Check chunker version, embedding model, vector dimension, and active index generation.
Verify that the embedding backlog contains the new segment digest.
Check whether text was redacted or excluded under policy.
Do not broaden the search into personal or unattributed corpora automatically.
Do not regenerate the original session from a summary to make the search test pass.
Evidence: source range, chunk identity, embedding state, and the evaluation query.
Recovery: replay derived indexing from the canonical archive and re-run both direct and semantic retrieval.

### 27.11 Search result exists but full transcript is missing

Symptom: an index preview is returned but its supporting source range cannot be opened.
Treat the result as incomplete evidence immediately.
Check the archive reference, retention tombstones, migration source completeness, and access policy.
Distinguish authorization rejection from actual missing storage.
Do not show a preview as a full transcript.
Do not remove the completeness warning because the search score is high.
Reconcile the derived index against retained archive manifests.
Evidence: result ID, source reference, catalog state, and the precise missing range.
Recovery: restore from an authorized verified backup when available; otherwise retain the gap and repair the index projection.
A missing original is not recovered by paraphrasing a surviving summary.

### 27.12 Spot worker disappears before shutdown finishes

Symptom: Pod or node vanishes while drain or checkpoint upload was in progress.
Read the latest complete checkpoint, not the most recently started checkpoint.
Read the last durable transcript cursor separately.
Determine whether the old generation is fenced and whether external effects remain ambiguous.
Do not assume the entire task state survived because the cloud interruption notice was observed.
Restore only verified objects from the complete manifest.
Choose qualified native resume, explicit context continuation, or explicit fresh execution.
The successor rereads the authoritative ledger before acting.
Evidence: last complete checkpoint sequence, missing tail interval, and restore decision.
Recovery: admit one successor generation and keep the original loss report linked to the task.

### 27.13 Native resume fails

Symptom: the new harness cannot open the original native conversation.
Check harness version compatibility, expected account binding, session artifact completeness, and path requirements.
Check whether the checkpoint was consistent or explicitly partial.
Do not retry indefinitely against an incompatible format.
Do not silently switch accounts to obtain a successful launch.
Do not label a new conversation as a native resume.
The operator/master sees a bounded decision with the available evidence and remaining workspace state.
Evidence: sanitized provider error, version tuple, native session identity, and checkpoint constraints.
Recovery: repair a supported compatibility issue or select a separately labelled continuation mode.
The task remains assigned through the current generation, not through the old PID.

### 27.14 Brain injects the wrong project's context

Symptom: an agent in one repository receives another repository's arcs, lessons, or inferred intent.
Check the source ProjectIdentity, canonical project key, brain binding, and current task generation.
Check exact metadata filters in the feed and search paths.
Check cache keys and evidence revisions.
Check graph traversal scope at every expansion step.
Check whether a historical unscoped entry was incorrectly promoted to a project by a text mention.
Pause scoped injection for the affected route while preserving approved shared-infrastructure alerts.
Do not mask the defect by hiding all brain context forever.
Evidence: sanitized request/response IDs, project bindings, selected item IDs, and selection explanations.
Recovery: fix attribution or routing, invalidate the affected scope cache, and rerun two-project isolation tests.

### 27.15 Personal/swarm brain isolation violation

Symptom: a swarm principal can read personal knowledge or one brain lifecycle action affects another.
Treat this as an isolation incident, not a relevance-quality issue.
Stop the affected cross-scope route and revoke compromised grants according to policy.
Check namespaces, vault paths, database/schema credentials, Redis prefixes, container names, and discovery selectors.
Check whether a client changed brain selection through mutable local configuration.
Preserve audit evidence without copying the leaked private content into a public issue.
Do not run a global compose teardown as cleanup.
Evidence: instance identities, authorization decision, affected data categories, and lifecycle target resolution.
Recovery: restore narrow bindings and qualify negative access/lifecycle tests before reenabling the route.
Notify the operator with an explicit description of the affected boundary and evidence limitations.

### 27.16 Brain graph returns obsolete advice

Symptom: an old decision is returned as current guidance despite a superseding decision.
Read the full decision records and directional `supersedes` relationship.
Check graph projection revisions and the active context cache.
Check whether an arbitrary edge-type priority discarded the supersession relation.
Check whether the relation is candidate or verified.
Do not erase historical decisions merely to hide a retrieval problem.
Keep historical content available as history with a visible successor link.
Evidence: original and successor IDs, revisions, relation evidence, and returned context explanation.
Recovery: repair the relation/projection and qualify the supersession evaluation cases.
Only the explicitly accepted current decision should guide the present protected transition.

### 27.17 Brain consultation gate is blocking valid work

Symptom: the agent has retrieved context but the next protected transition is refused.
Check receipt authenticity, execution binding, task generation, project, operation class, expiry, and delivery acknowledgement.
Check whether the task phase changed after the lookup.
Check whether the provider supports the hook event used for delivery.
Distinguish a fresh empty result from an unavailable service.
Do not satisfy the gate with a fabricated marker or arbitrary tool-call count.
An operator override uses the existing approved override path with scope, reason, and expiry.
Evidence: receipt ID and validation reason without exposing protected context bodies.
Recovery: deliver a valid scoped context pack or apply the explicit degraded-mode policy.
A successful override does not weaken unrelated secrets, branch, or infrastructure controls.

### 27.18 Brain service is unavailable

Symptom: context lookup times out or returns a dependency-unavailable error.
Read the selected brain binding and service health without switching instances automatically.
Use last-known-good context only within its declared freshness and scope policy.
For a protected transition, apply the configured unavailable policy rather than treating it as no matching memory.
Keep transcript capture and local task evidence running where safe.
Bound retries and prevent a wave of workers from causing a retry storm.
Do not terminate all agents merely because a semantic retrieval dependency is briefly down.
Evidence: request IDs, failure category, cache age, and gate decision.
Recovery: restore the dependency, refresh context, and invalidate temporary overrides when they expire.
Record whether work continued in degraded mode and which constraints remained enforced.

### 27.19 Worker image rollout would restart active tasks

Symptom: GitOps detects a new image or secret and attempts broad worker replacement.
Verify ownership: long-lived service rollout differs from controller-owned execution attempts.
Existing attempts retain their admitted image digest unless an explicit drain operation is authorized.
New attempts use the new qualified image after compatibility checks.
Check that automatic reloader annotations are not inherited blindly from long-lived service charts.
Do not mutate a running attempt's toolchain in place to match a moving tag.
Evidence: old/new image digests, affected attempts, and controller admission policy.
Recovery: stop the unqualified rollout, retain existing attempts, and qualify a new canary.
A security emergency may justify forced retirement, but the data-loss risk and authority revocation must be explicit.

### 27.20 Idle nodes cannot scale down

Symptom: swarm work is complete but eligible cloud capacity remains unnecessarily active.
Check completed or orphaned Pods, active reservations, drain state, and eviction-protection annotations.
Check whether an unrelated workload legitimately needs the node.
Check autoscaler's configured delay and unneeded classification before declaring a defect.
Remove only verified completed execution objects through the controller cleanup path.
Do not terminate a node directly to bypass a still-active workload's protection.
Evidence: object ownership, task completion, reservation release, and autoscaler reasoning.
Recovery: repair cleanup or annotation lifecycle and verify scale-down with an isolated canary.
A cost dashboard must distinguish stopped warm-pool storage from running instance capacity.

### 27.21 Data restore or index rebuild

Symptom: a durable store needs restoration or a derived index must be rebuilt.
Identify whether the missing component is authoritative source, catalog, knowledge, or a derived projection.
Restore authoritative data to an isolated target first.
Verify hashes, manifest references, scope bindings, and representative retrieval results.
Rebuild derived indexes from the restored authoritative stores.
Do not start coding agents merely to repopulate a search index.
Do not mix a personal database with swarm credentials during a restore.
Record the recovery point and any source gaps beyond it.
Evidence: backup identifiers, restore target, validation results, and cutover decision.
Recovery: switch the selected endpoint or index generation only after qualified read verification.
Retain the previous target until the rollback policy permits retirement.

### 27.22 Retired transcript endpoint still receives traffic

Symptom: callers still attempt to use the retired search endpoint after cutover.
Inventory the actual callers through sanitized routing telemetry.
Classify each as an active supported integration, stale configuration, or unauthorized use.
Migrate supported session-search consumers to the agentihooks session API/MCP contract.
Do not restore the old dispatcher, registry, or general-purpose runtime as a compatibility shortcut.
A temporary compatibility alias, when explicitly approved, must terminate in the new scoped read-only session implementation.
Give any alias an expiry, owner, and usage metric.
Evidence: caller inventory, required search method, and migrated configuration.
Recovery: remove the remaining obsolete configuration and rerun dependency audits.
The final architecture contains no runtime dependency on the retired service.

<a id="section-28"></a>

## 28. Release evidence, privacy, and completion checklists

### 28.1 Publication is not implementation completion

Committing this plan creates the specification artifact only.
