Creating an issue creates the execution tracker only.
Neither action satisfies the runtime, memory, brain, or infrastructure acceptance gates.
The issue remains open until the required evidence is linked and the operator accepts the verified scope.
Every test in section 21 is specified work to implement, not a reported execution result.
A structural validation report for this document validates the document, not the distributed system.

### 28.2 Code and deployment evidence

Record the accepted plan revision or document hash.
Record the exact tested agentihooks commit.
Record the exact tested agentibrain-kernel commit.
Record the exact tested antoncore commit.
Record qualified worker and service image digests.
Record the configuration revision and selected policy versions.
Record the migration versions and their rollback constraints.
Record the test environment and whether each proof is mocked, local integration, or live canary.
Record every failed canary that affected the final design.
Record any deviations as explicit accepted architecture decisions.
Do not discard failures merely because a later attempt passed.

### 28.3 Privacy review before committing reports

Remove operational network addresses from plan-derived public reports.
Remove provider token values, refresh tokens, private keys, and secret-store payloads.
Remove private transcript bodies unless the operator explicitly permits publication.
Use synthetic session examples in tests committed to public repositories.
Replace internal object references with sanitized stable placeholders in public evidence summaries.
Do not replace the real evidence in its protected store; keep a mapping under appropriate access control.
Check that summaries do not leak hidden project names or personal-brain material.
Check that screenshots do not expose credentials or unrelated terminal content.
Check that dependency source links are permitted for the intended repository audience.
A private repository source URL is a pointer, not a copy of its protected content.

### 28.4 Final operator walkthrough

Start a local-only swarm and prove unchanged supported behavior.
Start a single approved Kubernetes worker and inspect it in the Anton-hosted herdr client.
Close the viewer and prove the same worker continues.
Reconnect and verify execution identity and native conversation identity.
Start bounded pending work and observe scaling through the existing autoscaler.
Show that a request without the required tolerations does not access reserved capacity.
Demonstrate Claude and Codex transcript search against exact project filters.
Open a result's original supporting record range from durable storage after its worker has gone.
Open two different projects and show different scoped brain context.
Show an applicable shared-infrastructure warning reaching both authorized project sessions.
Retrieve a historical lesson through an approved graph relationship.
Show that an obsolete decision is identified as superseded.
Show the consultation receipt and supported hook delivery for a protected transition.
Show that no new lesson is acceptable when the task produced no novel learning.
Demonstrate personal/swarm separation for both search and lifecycle actions.
Rehearse a worker loss with a visible, truthful restore decision and one current writer.
Show archive and checkpoint watermarks separately.
Show idle execution cleanup and bounded capacity release.
Show the final runtime dependency inventory.
Link each demonstrated result to the package and acceptance gate it satisfies.

### 28.5 Maintenance ownership

The agentihooks maintainer owns runtime adapter compatibility and transcript normalizer versions.
The brain maintainer owns attribution, graph semantics, context policy, and knowledge migrations.
The antoncore maintainer owns cluster delivery, private networking, secrets integration, and capacity policies.
A release owner coordinates version tuples across repositories.
An operations owner verifies backups and restore drills.
A security owner reviews credential scope and personal/swarm isolation failures.
The operator owns spending ceilings and approval of new infrastructure pools.
Provider CLI updates require compatibility qualification before entering the default worker image.
An embedding-model change requires retrieval evaluation and an index-generation migration.
A brain-policy change requires injection and gate regression tests.
A new agent harness must implement the normalization and delivery capability contracts instead of changing provider-neutral orchestration.

### 28.6 Explicitly deferred features

Cross-brain automatic federation is not required for this baseline.
Cross-brain export/import can be added later only through explicit authorization and provenance rules.
One brain per worker is not a target feature.
A dedicated memory-optimized ASG is optional future infrastructure work, not an implied existing dependency.
A new compute pool for swarm-only workloads is optional until coexistence evidence requires it.
A custom graph database is not required while the bounded relational traversal meets the qualified workload.
A second coding-task queue or execution autoscaler is not a deferred default; it would require an architectural change.
A web terminal replacement is not required if the Anton-hosted herdr client and ledger satisfy operator needs.
Automated production spending increases remain outside the admitted baseline.

### 28.7 Program closure conditions

All mandatory work packages have evidence or an explicit operator-approved equivalent replacement decision.
Every applicable acceptance gate is satisfied in the declared environment.
No mandatory failure case is hidden by a generic success label.
The local execution fallback is qualified.
The durable source archive is independently restorable.
The brain project-scoping issue is satisfied or linked to the accepted successor implementation with its tests.
The retired transcript service is absent from the deployed target dependency graph.
The final issue summary states what is implemented, what is qualified, and what remains deliberately unsupported.
The operator can identify the accepted release tuple and its rollback path without reconstructing this conversation.

### 29.1 Source descriptions

#### SRC-AH-GUIDE: agentihooks: `CLAUDE.md`

Reference: [SRC-AH-GUIDE].
Repository entry points, target adapters, testing conventions, existing hook integration, and local-process assumptions. Re-read before editing because the development branch can advance.

#### SRC-AH-STORE: agentihooks: `scripts/swarm/store.py`

Reference: [SRC-AH-STORE].
Existing swarm configuration, task claims, leases, agent records, seats, naming, and handoff storage. This is the extension seam, not permission to create another task authority.

#### SRC-AH-RUNTIME: agentihooks: `scripts/swarm/runtime.py`

Reference: [SRC-AH-RUNTIME].
Existing local herdr runtime and launch/resume/retire behavior. Distributed target selection is proposed work in this plan.

#### SRC-AH-TERMINATE: agentihooks: `scripts/terminate_agent.py`

Reference: [SRC-AH-TERMINATE].
Existing local process-table discovery, process identity validation, termination, and pane closure. Local PID checks must remain local observations.

#### SRC-AH-LEDGER: agentihooks: `scripts/swarm_ledger/ledger.py`

Reference: [SRC-AH-LEDGER].
Existing HTTP ledger calls and local HTML token lookup. The v2 credential and remote-worker path must remove the local-file dependency without removing authorization.

#### SRC-AH-IDENTITY: agentihooks: `hooks/context/project_identity.py`

Reference: [SRC-AH-IDENTITY].
Current project resolution using Git common-directory information, repository remote, swarm context, and scratch-folder conventions. Preserve the client-side work already shipped.

#### SRC-AH-READER: agentihooks: `hooks/memory/transcript_reader.py`

Reference: [SRC-AH-READER].
Unified Claude, Codex, and Copilot record normalization. Reuse normalization while adding an incremental, durable source-capture contract.

#### SRC-AH-NORMALIZER: agentihooks: `hooks/targets/normalizer.py`

Reference: [SRC-AH-NORMALIZER].
Provider hook normalization and native transcript discovery. Actual provider capabilities must remain explicit instead of inferred from a common tool name.

#### SRC-AH-SNAPSHOT: agentihooks: `scripts/swarm/snapshot.py`

Reference: [SRC-AH-SNAPSHOT].
Existing snapshot contains coordination state, a ledger copy, and worktree path mappings. It does not by itself archive worktree contents or native conversation stores.

#### SRC-AH-MEMORY: agentihooks: `hooks/memory/store.py`

Reference: [SRC-AH-MEMORY].
Existing keyword memory store and local fallback. It is not a complete semantic transcript archive and should not be described as one.

#### SRC-AH-PROJECT-CACHE: agentihooks: `hooks/context/project_cache.py`

Reference: [SRC-AH-PROJECT-CACHE].
Current client-side project-memory cache, rendering, and deferred refresh. Multi-brain and task-specific cache keys are proposed extensions.

#### SRC-BRAIN-ARCS: agentibrain-kernel: `services/mcp/app/tools/arcs.py`

Reference: [SRC-BRAIN-ARCS].
Current semantic arc lookup and limited detail retrieval. Graph expansion and full source-backed detail are separate v2 requirements.

#### SRC-BRAIN-CLI: agentibrain-kernel: `docs/CLI.md`

Reference: [SRC-BRAIN-CLI].
Current whole-machine lifecycle and one-stack-per-machine convention. Named-instance isolation changes must avoid tearing down another installed brain.

#### SRC-BRAIN-CONFIG: agentibrain-kernel: `agentibrain/config.py`

Reference: [SRC-BRAIN-CONFIG].
Current environment/file configuration and brain home resolution. The v2 instance binding must be explicit and isolated.

#### SRC-BRAIN-COMPOSE: agentibrain-kernel: `agentibrain/templates/compose/compose.yml.j2`

Reference: [SRC-BRAIN-COMPOSE].
Current compose services, fixed container names, vault mounts, and pipeline cadence. Same-host multi-instance support must remove collisions deliberately.

#### SRC-BRAIN-EXTRACT: agentibrain-kernel: `services/brain-ops/extract.py`

Reference: [SRC-BRAIN-EXTRACT].
Current Claude-oriented extraction and working-folder project derivation. The target consumes normalized session evidence with canonical identity.

#### SRC-BRAIN-CLUSTER: agentibrain-kernel: `services/brain-ops/cluster.py`

Reference: [SRC-BRAIN-CLUSTER].
Current project/time grouping, cluster creation, source-session links, and sibling discovery. Task lineage must prevent unrelated simultaneous tasks from collapsing into one arc.

#### SRC-BRAIN-FEED: agentibrain-kernel: `services/brain-api/app/feed.py`

Reference: [SRC-BRAIN-FEED].
Current feed file reader and global payload generation. Project-level selection must happen before the top-N truncation.

#### SRC-BRAIN-EDGES: agentibrain-kernel: `services/brain-ops/brain_apply.py`

Reference: [SRC-BRAIN-EDGES].
Existing relation application and edge deduplication behavior. Preserve evidence and directional semantics when replacing the strongest-type-per-pair heuristic.

#### SRC-BRAIN-EMBED: agentibrain-kernel: `services/brain-ops/embed_arcs.py`

Reference: [SRC-BRAIN-EMBED].
Existing arc and daily-lesson indexing. V2 adds exact scope metadata, full evidence references, and entry-level lesson retrieval.

#### SRC-BRAIN-TICK: agentibrain-kernel: `services/brain-ops/brain_tick_prompt.py`

Reference: [SRC-BRAIN-TICK].
Current bounded reasoning prompt, edge suggestions, intent, and arc synthesis. Context consultation does not require running a full global tick per tool call.

#### SRC-ANTON-ASG: antoncore: `stacks/terraform/modules/ec2-arc-runners/asg.tf`

Reference: [SRC-ANTON-ASG].
Existing ASG names, launch-template integration, warm-pool policy, node-template tags, and desired-capacity ownership. Refer to the source without copying operational addresses.

#### SRC-ANTON-VARS: antoncore: `stacks/terraform/modules/ec2-arc-runners/variables.tf`

Reference: [SRC-ANTON-VARS].
Declared capacity ceilings and equal-shape instance alternatives. These values are source declarations, not measured live capacity or spending approval.

#### SRC-ANTON-CA: antoncore: `k8s/charts/cluster-autoscaler/values.yaml`

Reference: [SRC-ANTON-CA].
Existing autoscaler priorities, node discovery, provisioning timeout, and scale-down configuration. A swarm overlay must not alter unrelated workload behavior accidentally.

#### SRC-ANTON-JOIN: antoncore: `automation/packer/files/anton-k3s-join.sh`

Reference: [SRC-ANTON-JOIN].
Existing private-network join, lifecycle-state handling, and AWS provider identity. Node bootstrap remains separate from the worker container.

#### SRC-BRAIN-89: Existing project-scoped memory issue

Reference: [SRC-BRAIN-89].
Rechecked open during preparation. Defines kernel attribution, marker persistence, exact search filters, project feeds, project intent, and Codex extraction; it also records the shipped client-side work.

#### SRC-LEGACY-SEARCH: Extraction-only reference: retired transcript semantic-search logic

Reference: [SRC-LEGACY-SEARCH].
Only a source for the useful turn-chunking and vector-search implementation ideas. No runtime, dispatcher, registry, authentication server, or deployment dependency is retained from this project.

#### SRC-HERDR-MACHINES: herdr remote machines

Reference: [SRC-HERDR-MACHINES].
Remote server ownership, machine-scoped identifiers, SSH connectivity, and a shared operator client.

#### SRC-HERDR-CLI: herdr CLI

Reference: [SRC-HERDR-CLI].
Headless server operation and machine-qualified command surface. Verify supported command flags against the selected pinned release.

#### SRC-K8S-LIFECYCLE: Kubernetes Pod lifecycle

Reference: [SRC-K8S-LIFECYCLE].
Pod identity, termination, and runtime lifetime. Recreating a Pod does not preserve its former processes.

#### SRC-K8S-AUTOSCALING: Kubernetes node autoscaling

Reference: [SRC-K8S-AUTOSCALING].
Unschedulable workload requests and eligible node templates drive capacity decisions.

#### SRC-K8S-RESOURCES: Kubernetes resource management

Reference: [SRC-K8S-RESOURCES].
Requests, limits, and scheduling/resource-enforcement distinctions. Measure real worker process trees before production sizing.

#### SRC-K8S-STATEFULSET: Kubernetes StatefulSets

Reference: [SRC-K8S-STATEFULSET].
Stable service identity is distinct from a controller-owned ephemeral execution attempt.

#### SRC-K8S-RBAC: Kubernetes RBAC

Reference: [SRC-K8S-RBAC].
Separate controller permissions from worker permissions and constrain allowed API operations.

#### SRC-K8S-SECRETS: Kubernetes Secrets

Reference: [SRC-K8S-SECRETS].
Credential delivery and its security limitations. Merely using a Secret is not the entire isolation design.

#### SRC-K8S-NETWORK: Kubernetes NetworkPolicies

Reference: [SRC-K8S-NETWORK].
Network isolation requires a supporting implementation and explicit allowed traffic.

#### SRC-PGVECTOR: pgvector upstream documentation

Reference: [SRC-PGVECTOR].
Vector indexing, filtered retrieval, and tuning behavior. Use scoped evaluation rather than assuming an index provides authorization.

#### SRC-AWS-SPOT: AWS Spot interruption notices

Reference: [SRC-AWS-SPOT].
Interruption notices and available handling time. Design for loss without a completed shutdown as well.

#### SRC-REDIS-LOCKS: Redis distributed locking

Reference: [SRC-REDIS-LOCKS].
Ownership, expiry, and distributed lock assumptions. The plan additionally requires fencing at protected mutation boundaries.

### 29.2 Source refresh policy

A changed source file does not automatically invalidate the entire plan.
Compare the affected implementation seam and update the corresponding packages and contract fixtures.
Record source drift before beginning a live canary.
Retain the accepted original plan revision so implementation decisions remain auditable.
Do not copy confidential source content or operational addresses into this public-facing plan during refresh.
The existing project-scoping issue should be cross-linked rather than replaced by a duplicate issue.

<a id="section-30"></a>

## 30. End-of-plan completion statement

This document defines the full implementation program across agentihooks, agentibrain-kernel, and antoncore.
It preserves the working local swarm while adding qualified elastic execution, durable cross-harness memory, and scoped active brains.
The work-package and scenario counts describe specified work, not completed code or executed tests.
Production changes require the gate evidence and operator policies identified throughout the plan.
The canonical requested repository destination is root `Swarm-v2.md` on `agentihooks/dev`.
Publication and implementation completion are separate events.
